plain: We could not follow it from year to year: in single WISE epochs it is too faint or sits on other stars, so its motion is not measured here. Stacking all WISE images along its catalog motion (0.24 arcseconds per year) does show it (signal-to-noise 69), so it is there, just too faint to follow year by year.
Its infrared colour W1-W2 = 0.46 mag is normal for a star, not a cold brown dwarf.
Its brightness changes, but without a regular pattern (irregular variable).
Its SPHEREx spectrum is closest to one of the warmest templates (sdM9.5), but its 1.4 micrometre water band is shallower than a sdM9.5's: probably an ordinary star, warmer than the ultracool dwarfs.
